device: grid-scale iron-air battery (aqueous alkaline, shared iron electrode for charge and discharge)
failure: standard practice plateaus around 40-50% round-trip efficiency because the charge step competes with hydrogen evolution on the SAME iron electrode at ambient temperature — the parasitic reaction is fundamental to operating one electrocatalytically mediocre surface in both directions in an aqueous electrolyte; better cell engineering of the same shared-electrode architecture has not broken the plateau
constraint: earth-abundant materials only (no platinum-group or rare-earth catalysts); aqueous electrolyte; ambient temperature and pressure; >=1000 cycles; no addition of a separate third electrode for charge (that is the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism)
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism (not better engineering of the shared-electrode architecture) that could lift round-trip efficiency above 65% while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus near ZT ~1 at room-temperature-difference scales because electrical and thermal conductivity are carried by the same electrons — the Wiedemann-Franz relation ties them together, so decades of doping and alloying moved ZT only marginally; the coupling is fundamental to electron transport in a single-phase crystalline solid
constraint: solid-state (no moving parts, no working fluid, no Stirling cycle); hot side <= 250 C; must maintain ZT over >= 5000 h without degradation; contact/interfacial engineering alone is NOT a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that decouples electrical from thermal transport enough to reach ZT >= 2 while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus near 2.5-3.5 kWh/m3 (versus the ~1 kWh/m3 thermodynamic minimum) because the entire feed stream is pressurized to brine-recovery pressure and the residual brine pressure is then throttled away in one stage — the loss is fundamental to whole-feed single-stage pressurization with fixed membranes; incremental energy-recovery devices have already captured most of what that architecture allows
constraint: must remain pressure-driven membrane separation (no thermal distillation, no forward-osmosis regeneration loop); brine salinity <= 2x feed; capital cost within ~1.5x current RO trains; seawater feed
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that closes the gap toward 1.5 kWh/m3 while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus near 1-2C sustained charging without lithium plating because the anode's solid-state lithium diffusion is the rate limit — the surface potential dips below the plating threshold long before the graphite bulk can absorb the incoming flux; electrode thinning, coating, and electrolyte additives have shifted the plateau only marginally in a decade
constraint: cell-level energy density >= 200 Wh/kg; >= 1000 cycles at the fast-charge rate; graphite-dominant anode (silicon <= 10 wt%); liquid electrolyte; no preheating above 60 C (brief preheat to 60 C is the incumbent workaround, not a new mechanism)
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that enables 4C sustained charge without plating while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: utility-scale silicon PV module in still-air climates
failure: standard practice loses roughly 10-15% of nameplate output on hot still days because cell efficiency falls about 0.3-0.4%/C while passive radiative-plus-convective cooling saturates near 30-40 C above ambient — the ceiling is fundamental to air's low heat-transfer coefficient and the ~300 K radiative sink; finning and airflow channels already sit at that ceiling
constraint: no water, no fans, no active cooling power; no tracking system; added cost <= 10% of module cost; 25-year outdoor life; must work at peak insolation with zero wind
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that keeps cells within 15 C of ambient at peak sun while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at 20-25 year gearbox life because every gust and torque transient passes through a fixed-ratio mesh — the fatigue accumulation on the same tooth surfaces is fundamental to rigidly coupling a fluctuating prime mover to a constant-speed generator; the incumbent alternatives (direct-drive mass/cost penalty, hydraulic drivetrain) are known and not the answer here
constraint: rotor rating 10 MW; tower-head mass budget of a geared 10 MW machine; no superconducting generator; gearbox-ratio changes and bigger bearings are NOT new mechanisms; offshore salt environment
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that decouples the transient loads from the torque path while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at ~50-100 kW/rack with engineered fluorinated fluids because the working fluids that boil at the right temperature are expensive, high-GWP, or both — the plateau is fundamental to needing a single fluid that is simultaneously a good dielectric, a good boiling fluid, and environmentally benign; better fluorochemistry is incremental
constraint: dielectric strength >= 30 kV/mm; no water anywhere near the electronics; GWP < 10; fluid cost <= ~20 USD/kg; material compatibility with copper, aluminum, FR4 over 10 years
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism (not a new fluid blend) that reaches 200 kW/rack while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: 1.2 GPa-class structural steel for hydrogen pipelines and tanks
failure: standard practice plateaus near 1-1.2 GPa strength with acceptable hydrogen embrittlement resistance because the trap sites that immobilize hydrogen (dislocations, precipitates) also raise ductile-to-brittle transition and lower weldability — the tradeoff is fundamental to using the same microstructural features for both strength and trapping; alloying around it has stalled for decades
constraint: strength >= 1.2 GPa; weldable by standard field processes; embrittlement resistance >= 2x current 1 GPa pipeline steels in NACE testing; cost within 1.5x commodity HSLA; no austenitic wrap or cladding (that is the incumbent workaround)
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism for hydrogen-compatible high-strength steel that escapes the strength-vs-trapping tradeoff while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice cannot go far below ~0.8 t CO2 per tonne clinker because roughly 60% of that CO2 comes from calcining limestone itself (CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2) — the chemistry of the feedstock is fundamental to portland clinker; kiln efficiency, alternative fuels, and clinker substitution have already captured the addressable part and substitution is capped by early-strength requirements
constraint: must deliver a cementitious binder that passes current structural concrete standards (set time, 28-day strength, durability); feedstock must be abundant at the gigatonne scale; process temperature <= 900 C; carbon capture on the plant is NOT a new mechanism (it is the incumbent mitigation)
question: Propose a NEW binder chemistry/mechanism that meets structural concrete performance with <= 0.2 t CO2 per tonne binder while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus near 0.3-1.1 W/kg core loss in grain-oriented electrical steel because hysteresis and eddy losses in a METALLIC ferromagnet at grid frequency are tied to domain-wall motion and finite conductivity — the plateau is fundamental to the loss mechanisms of metallic ferromagnets; amorphous metals cut loss but saturate at ~1.5 T flux and cost more
constraint: operating flux density >= 1.7 T (to keep transformer mass/size near current designs); grid frequency; 40-year life; insulation-compatible winding temperature rise; amorphous ribbon cores are the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism for the magnetic core that halves core loss while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at ~10-15 dB return loss across the full sub-6 GHz band because a passive antenna's impedance bandwidth is bounded by its electrical size (the Chu/Bode-Fano limit) — handsets are electrically small at the low bands, so the match floor is fundamental to passive electrically-small radiators; matching networks add loss roughly proportional to the bandwidth they recover
constraint: antenna volume <= 5x10^4 mm3 (handset-scale); passive (no amplifiers in the radiating path); efficiency >= 40% at 700 MHz; must cover 0.7-3.8 GHz; frequency-selective surfaces or switched matching are the incumbent workarounds, not new mechanisms
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that beats the passive electrically-small antenna bandwidth floor while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus near 60-100 cycles/minute for fine-pitch placement because the rigid tool must decelerate, settle mechanically to sub-100-micron precision, then place — the settle time is fundamental to exciting structural resonances of a stiff moving beam and then waiting for ring-down; stiffer structures shift resonances up but ring just as long relative to cycle time
constraint: placement precision <= 100 micron; payloads <= 500 g; cycle work envelope 300 mm; no vision-servo'd final approach longer than 50 ms (that is the incumbent workaround); machine cost within 2x current assembly gantries
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that reaches 300 cycles/minute at 100-micron precision while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at material-removal rates limited by regenerative chatter because tool-tooth passing vibrations modulate chip thickness, which feeds back into cutting force at the next tooth — the instability is fundamental to closed-loop force feedback in flexible structures; chatter suppression by spindle-speed selection and tuned holders has captured what the architecture allows
constraint: standard carbide tooling; aluminum and titanium workpieces; spindle power <= 30 kW; machine stiffness within current machine-tool mass budgets; active magnetic bearings are the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that triples the stable material-removal rate while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: main shaft bearing of a heavy industrial gearbox
failure: standard practice plateaus at PV (pressure x velocity) values around 100-200 MPa-m/s for grease-lubricated rolling bearings because elastohydrodynamic film thickness collapses as speed and load rise together — the limit is fundamental to a lubricant film that must be sheared in the same contact that carries the load; ceramic hybrids and better greases moved the plateau marginally
constraint: rolling-element bearing (no hydrodynamic journal conversion); grease lubrication only (no oil circulation system); 40,000-hour life; radial load within standard housing envelopes; diamond-like-carbon coatings are the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that carries 500 MPa-m/s in a grease-lubricated rolling contact while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at 15-25 year joint life because every thermal cycle ratchets the joint through full travel while traffic pounds the same mechanical interfaces — the wear accumulation is fundamental to a joint that must absorb large displacements AND carry wheel loads through the same moving parts; better elastomers and modular steel joints have both stalled at the same plateau
constraint: movement capacity +/- 500 mm; must carry highway legal loads including 40-tonne trucks; installation windows <= 8 hours overnight; no traffic rerouting for more than one night; routine replacement is the incumbent answer, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism for a 75-year-life expansion joint while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: tissue-engineered thick (>5 mm) bone scaffold implant
failure: standard practice plateaus at viable tissue depths of ~1-2 mm inside scaffolds because oxygen diffusion through avascular porous matrix saturates around 100-200 micron from any perfused surface before capillary ingrowth catches up — the limit is fundamental to diffusion-dominated oxygen supply in the weeks before vascularization; growth-factor cocktails and porosity tuning have not broken the mm-scale barrier
constraint: implantable in a single surgery (no external perfusion port, no staged flap surgery); resorbable within 18 months; mechanical strength >= 10 MPa in compression at implantation; no live cells delivered from outside the patient's own marrow; pre-vascularization in a bioreactor is the incumbent workaround, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that makes 10 mm of scaffold core viable in one surgery while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: fully implantable physiological sensor (cardiac pressure monitor)
failure: standard practice plateaus at 5-10 year battery-limited implant life because the sensor's electronics and telemetry draw micro-watts continuously and no transcutaneous energy harvest delivers that reliably deep in the chest — the limit is fundamental to far-field coupling into small implanted antennas under tissue loss; battery chemistry improvements add years, not decades
constraint: fully implanted (no percutaneous leads or wires); implant volume <= 3 cm3; must survive MRI at 1.5 T and 3 T; tissue temperature rise <= 1 C everywhere; inductive recharging by a worn vest is the incumbent workaround, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that powers the sensor for >= 30 years in vivo while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: hypersonic vehicle leading edge (Mach 5+, 0-degree bluntness class)
failure: standard practice plateaus at heat fluxes near 5-10 MW/m2 for sharp reusable leading edges because passive TPS conduction-radiation balance saturates at roughly 1500-1600 C material limits while sharper edges concentrate the flux — the ceiling is fundamental to radiating to a 300 K sky from a material that must also carry load; blunt edges (the incumbent answer) trade drag for survival and are not a new mechanism
constraint: reusable (>= 100 cycles); leading-edge radius <= 5 mm; no ablative or transpirative coolant (ablatives are expendable, transpiration needs a tank — both incumbent workarounds); structural load path through the edge itself; oxidation-resistant in dissociated air
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism for a sharp reusable leading edge at 10 MW/m2 while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at 1-3 year VLEO missions because drag make-up consumes propellant linearly with time and every kg of propellant displaces payload — the ceiling is fundamental to chemical propellant's low specific impulse for a continuous small-thrust mission; electric thrusters improve the exponent but still need propellant mass that scales with mission length
constraint: no nuclear systems; propellant mass <= 15% of satellite mass; attitude control must survive continuous thrusting; optical payload aperture >= 40 cm; deployable aerodynamic surfaces are the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism enabling 10-year VLEO missions while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus at 400-500 C and 150-300 bar because the iron/ruthenium catalyst needs extreme N2 activation energy that only high temperature supplies, and conversion equilibrium then needs high pressure to overcome the entropy penalty — the severity is fundamental to catalytic N2 dissociation on metal surfaces; a century of catalyst tuning has moved conditions only modestly
constraint: N2 from air, H2 from electrolysis (green); synthesis loop capital <= 1/3 of a Haber-Bosch train at the same daily tonnage; catalyst cost within 3x of promoted-iron per kg NH3; product anhydrous ammonia (no carrier chemicals); plasma or electrochemical syntheses of record-low efficiency are the incumbent alternatives, not new mechanisms
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that synthesizes ammonia near 100 C and 10 bar while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

failure: standard practice plateaus near 40-60% lithium recovery over 12-24 months of evaporation because selective lithium transport competes with magnesium and potassium in the same brine as it concentrates — the loss is fundamental to evaporative concentration being non-selective and chemistry-blind; pre-treatment reagents capture some impurities but cannot change the evaporative base mechanism
constraint: no freshwater consumption beyond current operations; pond footprint must not grow; must handle Mg:Li ratios >= 10; product battery-grade (>= 99.5%); direct lithium extraction membranes are the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that reaches >= 85% lithium recovery in <= 2 months while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: flexible EMI shield for dense 5G/6G cable bundles
failure: standard practice plateaus near 40-60 dB shielding for shields below ~30 microns because reflection loss scales with conductivity-thickness product and absorption with thickness — the floor is fundamental to metallic conduction at sub-skin-depth thicknesses; thicker metallization or multilayer stacks is the incumbent answer and adds stiffness and cost
constraint: total shield thickness <= 15 microns; flexible (survive 10,000 bend cycles at 5 mm radius); shielding >= 80 dB from 1-40 GHz; weight <= 30 g/m2; must not rely on increasing metal thickness (the incumbent lever); carbon-based coatings are the incumbent alternative, not a new mechanism
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism for 80 dB shielding at <= 15 microns while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: soft pneumatic actuator for robotic manipulation
failure: standard practice plateaus at a speed-force ceiling because pneumatic soft actuators deliver large force only when highly pressurized chambers inflate slowly, while fast inflation destabilizes the chamber walls — the tradeoff is fundamental to gas as the force-transmission medium (low bulk modulus, compressible); hydraulics fixes stiffness but abandons softness/safety and is the incumbent alternative
constraint: intrinsic softness/safety (must not pinch harder than its own material stiffness — no high-modulus skeletons); power density >= 1 kW/m3 at the actuator; bandwidth >= 20 Hz at full force; payload-to-actuator-mass ratio >= 5; tendon drives and granular jamming are incumbent workarounds, not new mechanisms
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that breaks the speed-force ceiling of soft actuation while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.

device: insulated carbon-steel piping in a petrochemical unit (corrosion-under-insulation)
failure: standard practice plateaus at finding CUI only after wall loss exceeds ~1-2 mm because insulation must be stripped for visual/ultrasonic access, so programs sample only a few percent of surfaces — the blindness is fundamental to needing contact or line-of-sight through a barrier designed to block exactly that access; pulsed-eddy-current scans are the incumbent partial answer (limited depth resolution under insulation)
constraint: no insulation stripping (removal is the incumbent answer); detection of wall loss <= 0.2 mm from OUTSIDE the insulation; coverage of 100% of pipe length at walking pace; distinction between exterior CUI and interior flow corrosion; retrofit to existing units without shutdown
question: Propose a NEW physical mechanism that detects 0.2 mm wall loss through insulation while respecting every stated constraint, and state the concrete test that would falsify it.
